history.change: For AI agents: a new page, IQC-AG-01, describes the agent and its MCP server for AI agents and the people who build them, with llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and sitemap.xml beside it; agent steps traced back to sealed measurements, reviewer sign-off and the MCP server work today, so the Overview, the Roadmap (renumbered), Check a record, How a record is sealed and the Regulatory map no longer call them upcoming.

Patent guardrails: every item that would have put records or their fingerprints on a network, and any shared service for records, is removed from the plans and the pages. The record history stays a signed file the lab keeps; the anchor on these pages stays simulated, and in use it would be a fingerprint the lab pins by its own means. The Roadmap renumbers its items.
The Overview moved from index.html to overview.html, and a new landing page at index.html and the app at app/ replace the alpha console, whose old address now leads to the app.

Repositioned for automated research labs: the Scope names the audience; the Overview gains section 2, “Why: one wrong value snowballs”, with the founder’s line, redraws Where it fits for an automated lab (today beside an HPLC CSV export; sealing at the orchestrator or driver, upcoming), moves the regulatory position to “When your process moves into GMP” and renumbers the later sections; the Roadmap adds sealing at capture, measured and derived records, lineage and recall, Merkle batches with salted leaves and post-quantum signatures and encryption, and rewrites Filecoin integration as an encrypted archive on Filecoin, all Upcoming, with the automated-lab items first; How a record is sealed says a pass does not show that a value was ever measured, what a registry entry would show, and that nothing readable leaves the lab; About adds two questions, on the kinds of labs it is for and on sabotage and espionage, and folds “What does a fingerprint cover?” into the question on the orchestrator, ELN, CDS and LIMS.

The Overview gains section 2, “How a result becomes a sealed record”, which walks record 6 through seven animated steps (captured, fingerprinted, signed, linked, a change, a correction, and what is upcoming) with every value computed at build; the later sections and figures are renumbered.

Adds one upcoming item, signatures that cover each record’s position, so a removed or moved record shows without an anchor; How a record is sealed links to it. Today’s signatures still cover only each record’s own fingerprint, as in the alpha app.

Everything not built yet is labeled Upcoming, under one label, and the Scope states anchoring as upcoming; the status line no longer names a test network; the Roadmap lists nine upcoming items; on the Regulatory map, clause numbers stay only where confirmed and “Not covered” replaces “Not yet”; the alpha app’s capture time, and what a removed record shows, described as they are; a missing signature, or a field holding the separator, now fails its check; corrections need a reason of at least three words and, in the console too, carry the result’s capture time, not the time they were made; the console can simulate a deleted record; the set is marked informational, not a controlled document; GitHub Pages publishes only the built site, through GitHub Actions.

Full document set: every page written in full; Fig. 2 Record history on the Overview; one ring-and-dot mark for the nav, favicon and og card; the auditor’s link rule (a changed value breaks only the link into the next record); the privacy roadmap item; a regulatory map clause by clause; the alpha console reworked as an in-browser demo and linked again.
Prototype of the document set: Overview and Check a record in full; How a record is sealed, Regulatory map, Roadmap and About in outline. Not published.

copy.definition: Each result becomes a sealed record: a SHA-256 fingerprint of five of its recorded fields, signed and linked to the record before it, so a later change shows. Built for automated research labs in biotechnology, microbiology, chemistry and materials science, where results arrive faster than people can review them and models train on them. The records and their history stay with the lab; nothing is written to a network.
copy.whyNow: Most bad data is not malicious. But when results arrive faster than people can review them, and models train on them and choose the next experiment, an ordinary mistake travels before anyone sees it.
copy.status: Independent project · Open alpha · Synthetic demo data · No customers yet
copy.regulatory: Built toward the audit-trail expectations of 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11 and ISO/IEC 17025:2017. Not validated. No electronic signatures yet. Not a substitute for your computerized-system validation or SOPs.
copy.footer: Immutable QC is an independent project built on the founder’s own time. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any employer. Founder: José A. Fernández Abreu · joseqc.com
copy.independence: Immutable QC is an independent project built on the founder’s own time. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by any employer.
copy.demoSig: Demo signatures. In the alpha, one server key signs imported rows; per-analyst signatures are upcoming.
copy.founderLine: In an intelligence explosion, human review can’t keep up with every result; records have to verify themselves.
